articles.excerpt: 비트코인과 함께 시작된 블록체인 패러다임은 탈중앙화, 투명성, 불변성을 갖춘 장부 시스템을 약속했다. 하지만 확장성, 프라이버시, 상호운용성이라는 내재된 한계로 인해 광범위한 채택에 지속적으로 어려움을 겪었다. 탈중앙화, 보안, 확장성을 동시에 달성하기 어려운 '블록체인 트릴레마'는 개발자와 사용자 모두에게 끊임없는 난관이었다. 다양한 레이어 1 및 레이어…
articles.body: 비트코인과 함께 시작된 블록체인 패러다임은 탈중앙화, 투명성, 불변성을 갖춘 장부 시스템을 약속했다. 하지만 확장성, 프라이버시, 상호운용성이라는 내재된 한계로 인해 광범위한 채택에 지속적으로 어려움을 겪었다. 탈중앙화, 보안, 확장성을 동시에 달성하기 어려운 '블록체인 트릴레마'는 개발자와 사용자 모두에게 끊임없는 난관이었다. 다양한 레이어 1 및 레이어 2 솔루션이 이러한 문제 해결을 위해 등장했지만, 영지식 증명(ZK-proofs)만큼 혁신적인 잠재력을 지닌 것은 드물다. 영지식 증명은 한 당사자(증명자)가 다른 당사자(검증자)에게 어떤 진술이 사실임을, 그 진술의 진실성 외에는 어떤 정보도 드러내지 않고 확신시킬 수 있도록 하는 혁명적인 암호학적 원시 기술이다. 겉보기에는 역설적인 이 능력은 블록체인 기술의 새로운 지평을 열어, 거래가 처리되는 방식, 프라이버시가 유지되는 방식, 그리고 서로 다른 블록체인 네트워크가 상호작용하는 방식을 근본적으로 변화시킬 핵심을 쥐고 있다. 영지식 증명은 오프체인에서 검증 가능한 연산을 가능하게 하고, 방대한 양의 데이터를 간결한 증명으로 압축함으로써 블록체인 성장을 제약해왔던 핵심 병목 현상을 해결할 준비를 마쳤다. 이 글은 영지식 증명이 기존 블록체인 구조를 단순히 최적화하는 것을 넘어, 그 아키텍처를 근본적으로 재편하여 더욱 확장 가능하고 프라이빗하며 상호 연결된 탈중앙화된 미래를 위한 길을 어떻게 열어가는지 그 메커니즘을 깊이 탐구한다.

articles.title: How resume keyword matching actually works (and a free tool to check yours)
articles.excerpt: Most "your resume will be rejected by the ATS" advice is fear dressed up as fact. Here is what is actually going on, and what you can usefully check before you apply. When a recruiter searches their a…
articles.body: Most "your resume will be rejected by the ATS" advice is fear dressed up as fact. Here is what is actually going on, and what you can usefully check before you apply. What a keyword match is When a recruiter searches their applicant tracking system, they usually search for skills: Kubernetes , TypeScript , system design . Your resume shows up only if those words are in it. Whether a given company ranks or filters on them depends on how that company set its system up, and no outside tool can know that. What you can control is simple: if the job description asks for Kafka and you have used Kafka, the word Kafka should be on your resume, spelled the way the posting spells it. Three things that trip people up Synonyms you assume count.

articles.body: Building a Metaphysical Theory Reduction Engine: Applying Logic & Code to Consciousness Have you ever tried to map out every major theory of consciousness—from Reductive Physicalism to Analytic Idealism —and test their logical consistency? In the study of metaphysics and philosophy of mind, one recurring pattern emerges: most positive assertions about the fundamental nature of reality eventually run into logical contradictions or antinomies when pressed to their absolute limits. Inspired by the research of Peter Guy Jones (author of In Pursuit of the Inconceivable: An Investigation of Metaphysics and Mysticism , Essentia Books) and the taxonomies established by Robert Lawrence Kuhn ( Closer to Truth ), we built the Metaphysical Theory Reduction Engine (MTRE) .

articles.title: Why I Built SREK3S: An AI Incident Responder That Cannot Write to Your Cluster
articles.excerpt: / SREK3S SREK3S Most Kubernetes AI agents are a rootkit waiting to happen. They demand cluster-admin rights and stream raw stdout to external LLM APIs. SREK3S is a zero-trust, read-only incident respo…
articles.body: duckiec / SREK3S A fail-closed, AI-powered Site Reliability Engineer for your Kubernetes cluster. SREK3S Most Kubernetes AI agents are a rootkit waiting to happen. They demand cluster-admin rights and stream raw stdout to external LLM APIs. SREK3S is a zero-trust, read-only incident response agent. It intercepts pod crashes, scrubs secrets in-memory before network egress, and sandboxes LLM triage in a POSIX-jailed worker. It generates verified GitOps patches with strictly zero cluster write authority and deterministically fails closed to human review. Features Zero cluster mutations : namespaced get / list / watch only. No ClusterRole, no write field on either wire contract, no mounted token on the Agent. In-memory secret scrubbing : 11 ordered regex rules run before egress.

articles.title: How to Block OWASP Top 10 Attacks (Without Breaking Legitimate Traffic)
articles.excerpt: Most developers turn off Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) after getting flooded with false positives. Traditional rule engines often trigger immediate 403 Forbidden errors whenever a user uploads norm…
articles.body: Most developers turn off Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) after getting flooded with false positives. Traditional rule engines often trigger immediate 403 Forbidden errors whenever a user uploads normal text containing single quotes, HTML snippets, or complex search filters. Aegis integrates the Go-native Coraza WAF engine with the OWASP Core Rule Set (CRS v4) , using an intelligent cumulative anomaly scoring model rather than crude regex matching. Here is how to set it up and protect against SQLi, XSS, and RCE without breaking your application. What is Cumulative Anomaly Scoring? Instead of blocking on the very first pattern match, Aegis evaluates incoming requests across multiple detection vectors: A slightly unusual parameter might score 2 points (low anomaly).

articles.title: Mapping distributed data across microservices, without the API spam or replication?
articles.excerpt: Hi everyone, I recently ran into a problem with our microservices architecture: the data is spread across multiple services. For example, PatientId lives in Service A, but the actual patient info belo…
articles.body: Hi everyone, I recently ran into a problem with our microservices architecture: the data is spread across multiple services. For example, PatientId lives in Service A, but the actual patient info belongs to Service B. That's just a small example. I've got a ton of stuff to map, like master data, patient info, medicine info, and so on. I'd rather not write a bunch of API calls by hand or replicate data everywhere, so I've been working on a small library for it called FxMap. You declare what you need once with a fluent API, and it fetches and fills in the remote data over gRPC, RabbitMQ, Kafka, etc. It's still pretty young, so honest feedback is very welcome. Has anyone else dealt with this? Curious how you handled it, or if you'd do it differently.

articles.title: This app gives Wear OS the Pixel music feature Apple already copied
articles.excerpt: A new Wear OS app puts Pixel’s Now Playing where it always belonged.
articles.body: TL;DR Now On Wrist brings your Pixel’s Now Playing results directly to a Wear OS smartwatch. It can show detected songs through notifications, a watch face complication, and a dedicated Wear OS tile. The app is available now on Google Play and works with Wear OS 3.0 or newer. Hearing a great song and having your Pixel identify it automatically is handy, but checking the result still usually means reaching for your phone. That feels a little clunky when you’re already wearing a smartwatch, which is where a new app called Now On Wrist comes in. It fixes that disconnect by bringing your Pixel’s Now Playing results directly to Wear OS. Now On Wrist doesn’t actually turn your smartwatch into a music-recognition device.

articles.title: People really hate AI, so why can’t they get enough?
articles.excerpt: Over the summer I talked to the CEO of Springboards, a startup building an LLM that’s designed to come up with a wider variety of responses than its mainstream rivals do. At the start of the call, he…
articles.body: Over the summer I talked to the CEO of Springboards, a startup building an LLM that’s designed to come up with a wider variety of responses than its mainstream rivals do. At the start of the call, he said something that’s been stuck in my head since: “We often say that we’re a self-loathing AI company. We don’t know if we really like what we’re doing.” “I guess that makes me a self-loathing AI journalist,” I replied. It was a joke! I love my job. But I do not love many of the things the technology I write about has become: warped by hype , steered by zealots , inescapable . The CEO of Springboards and I are far from alone. Around the world, a love/hate attitude toward AI is very much the vibe right now. On the one hand, public feelings are souring fast.

articles.body: “I want to be able to look at a rocket launch and say, ‘I touched a piece of this.’” That’s how Richard Spolzino describes the thing he’s chasing. Not a title, not a specific mission, not even NASA itself, just the ability to point at something real and know his work made it possible. At NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, Spolzino works within Moon Base’s mission architecture and systems interoperability effort, helping identify what NASA still doesn’t know about the Moon and Mars, and making sure that missing information gets found before it becomes a problem.
